name: Malilla
description: Malilla is a point-trick game for four players in fixed partnerships, popular in Mexico and originating in Spain. Played with a 40-card Spanish deck, the Seven is the highest card (Malilla), ranking above Ace. Partners score card points (7=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one per trick; first team to 35 cumulative points wins. Trump is set by the dealer's last card turned face up.

overview.description: Malilla is a point-trick game for four players in fixed partnerships, popular in Mexico and originating in Spain. Played with a 40-card Spanish deck, the Seven is the highest card (Malilla), ranking above Ace. Partners score card points (7=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one per trick; first team to 35 cumulative points wins. Trump is set by the dealer's last card turned face up.

history.origins: Dates back to the 16th or 17th century. Its name is derived from the word for 'little bad one', referring to the powerful low-numbered cards.
timeline: 1600s: Mentioned in Spanish literature as a favorite among the nobility.
1800s: Spreads to the Spanish colonies in the Americas and the Philippines.
Present: Remains a traditional favorite in rural Spain and some Latin American regions.
20th Century: Largely superseded in popularity by games like Mus or Tute, but preserved in cultural heritage societies.
history.cultural: A game of social bonding, traditionally played in 'casinos' (private social clubs) in Spanish towns.
history.evolution: Spanish Malilla (Seven high) influenced the French game Manille (32-card, 10 high). Mexican Malilla keeps the 40-card Spanish pack with 7 as Malilla.

setup.deck: 40 cards: Suits are Oros (Coins), Copas (Cups), Espadas (Swords), Bastos (Clubs).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 10 cards. The dealer flips the last card to determine the Trump suit.

rules.objective: Your partnership must win tricks containing the high-value point cards (Seven=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one point per trick, and be the first team to reach 35 or more cumulative points to win the game.
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit if possible.
2. Must try to win the trick if possible (Overtake).
3. If unable to follow suit, you must play a trump card if you have one.
4. The winner of the trick leads the next.
keyRules: If an opponent is winning the trick, must beat their card if able (subject to follow suit).
When unable to follow suit, must play a trump if you have one.
Cannot discard a seven of a non-trump suit until that suit has been led to a trick.
Trump is the suit of the dealer's last card, turned face up. Winner of each trick leads to the next.

strategy.basic: Guard your Sevens (Malillas); each is worth 5 points. Do not discard a 7 of a non-trump suit until that suit has been led. Save high trumps for when you can capture point cards.
strategy.intermediate: Signal with leads: leading a low trump can ask partner to clear trumps. Track which 7s and Aces have been played to know what is still out.
strategy.advanced: Void a weak suit early so you can trump opponents' leads and capture their Aces and Kings. Coordinate with partner without communication by consistent carding.
tips: Memory is key: track which Sevens and high cards have been played.
When an opponent is winning the trick, you must beat their card if you can (subject to follow suit).

variations.name: Albur
variations.description: Before first deal, one player places two cards face down; opposing team chooses one. Higher card wins 5 points and mano (right to lead to first trick). Losers deal first.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Albur adds pre-deal mano bid; engine overrides to be added when implementing this variant.

variations.name: Manilla in Spain (48 cards)
variations.description: Played with 48 Spanish cards (eights and nines included). The nine is highest (Manilla), not the seven. Rank 9-1-12-11-10-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. 12 cards each, 12 tricks, 72 points total. Target 40 to win. No restriction on discarding a 9 of unled suit.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses 48-card deck and different rank order; deck and trump overrides to be added when implementing.

variations.name: Macau Manilla
variations.description: 40 cards from 52-card pack, rank 7-A-K-J-Q-10-9-8-6-5. Jack above Queen. Points 7=5, A=4, K=3, J=2, Q=1. No bonus for turned trump. No restriction on throwing non-trump manilla. Winning team scores difference; 70 points to win game.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Macau uses different rank order and target score; overrides to be added when implementing.

scoring.description: Card points (Seven=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one point per trick won (la negra). Total 70 points per deal. Team with more than 35 scores the difference; first to 35 cumulative wins.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach 35 or more cumulative points wins. Capote: win all 10 tricks to score 35 and win the game in one deal. Zapato: reach 35 while opponents have zero.
